title: Introduce affinity windowing and decentralize scheduler to reduce KV thrash
creator: Marco Alvarez
description:
Background: Over the last year we've observed recurrent KV cache eviction storms during mixed-tenancy bursts which amplify scheduler contention and increase tail latency. Current continuous-batching and prefetch heuristics treat all sessions uniformly which leads to cache thrash (hot key eviction, latency spikes), excessive cross-tenant lease churn, and higher CPU on the central scheduler.

Goal: Reduce KV eviction rate and scheduler contention by introducing an affinity-windowing layer that groups related requests (session/tenant/route affinity) into localized prefetch windows and by decentralizing admission decision logic from a single global scheduler to per-shard lightweight arbiters. This is a tech-debt refactor aimed at controlling memory churn and smoothing admission pressure while preserving batching efficiency and cache hit rates.

Scope: 
- Implement an affinity-windowing policy that allocates short-lived affinity buckets (time and token window-based) for flows that show locality.
- Add per-shard admission arbiters that enforce local concurrency limits and preference for affinity-cached sessions.
- Refactor prefetch path to expose a pluggable affinity hint API consumed by the KV priming layer.
- Migrate a subset of scheduler responsibilities (admission decisions, quick fairness heuristics) to shard arbiters; keep long-tail escape and global observability in the coordinator.
- Ensure backward compatibility via feature flags and runtime knobs; allow fallback to the global scheduler.

Why this approach: Affinity-windowing reduces redundant prefetch/eviction cycles by increasing temporal locality; per-shard arbiters reduce global lock contention and make admission decisions closer to the cache state, improving throughput and tail latency. Making the prefetch affinity pluggable keeps future experiments (e.g., tenant-weighted affinity, model-specific heuristics) straightforward.
tasks: Design affinity-window contract and API for prefetch hints
Prototype per-shard arbiter with in-memory counters and lease soft-limits
Implement affinity bucket lifecycle (creation, extension, teardown, eviction hook)
Refactor prefetch pipeline to accept and honor affinity hints
Instrument metrics: affinity_hits, affinity_evictions, arbiter_admissions, arbiter_rejects
Add feature flags and rollout gates: affinity_enabled, arbiter_mode
Create canary plan and load-test harness against 2-week production traffic replay
Rollout to canary shard group and monitor for regressions
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end canary run (72h) with affinity_enabled shows >= 30% reduction in KV eviction rate vs baseline
95th percentile tail latency for generation requests on canary shards does not increase; goal is <= 5% regression, target is no regression
Scheduler CPU on canary hosts reduces by >= 15% relative to baseline under bursty load
No customer-facing errors introduced (error budget not impacted during canary)
All new metrics emitted and dashboards created: affinity_hits, affinity_miss_ratio, arbiter_reject_rate
Fallback to global scheduler via simple toggle succeeds and restores previous behavior within 60s
risks: Affinity misclassification could concentrate pressure on a subset of shards and create local hotspots
Incorrect arbiter heuristics might starve low-volume customers if fairness isn't tuned
Bugs in migration/teardown could leave stale affinity state and leak memory
Instrumentation gaps could make regressions hard to detect quickly
mitigations: Start with conservative affinity window sizes and TTLs; run A/B with gradually increased window duration
Implement arbiter soft-limits and decay rules to prevent starvation; add a token-bucket fallback for fairness
Add comprehensive lifecycle tests for affinity bucket creation/GC and memory leak assertions
Ship dashboards and automated alerts for key indicators; maintain a rollback runbook
observability_plan: Affinity hit ratio per tenant and per route (histogram)
KV eviction rate tagged by affinity=true/false
Arbiter decisions: admits vs rejects with reason codes
End-to-end tracing span that annotates decisions with affinity bucket id
testing_plan: Unit tests for affinity bucket lifecycle and arbiter decision logic
Integration tests exercising feature flags, fallback paths, and GC
Replay-based load test using 7 days of production traffic (sanitized) to measure eviction and scheduler metrics
Chaos test: random arbiter failures and quick fallback to global scheduler
Memory/heap profiling during canary under sustained load
